body_markdown:
Most infrastructure organizations didn’t wait for an AI strategy. Their people started using Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot on their own, to draft reports, summarize contracts and answer questions about the work.


So the question for leaders has moved on. Your teams are using AI already. What is it reading when it answers?


### Fast answers from the wrong file


Point an AI tool at a shared drive and it will find something. Usually that’s the first spreadsheet that matches the question, or the tracker someone last saved in March. It reads the file quickly and answers with confidence.


The trouble is that infrastructure programs rarely have one version of anything. Lease status sits in one tracker, design approvals in another, survey results in a contractor’s inbox. Each copy drifts a little further from reality every week.


An AI tool can’t tell which version is current. It has no way of knowing that the site record it just quoted is three revisions out of date. You get a fast answer, and someone still has to check it before it goes anywhere near a board paper.


### The record matters more than the model


AI doesn’t improve your data. It reads it faster. A model that reasons brilliantly will still give a wrong answer from a wrong record.


That changes where the value sits. The organizations getting real returns from AI are the ones that fixed the foundation first: one place where every site, asset, task and document lives, owned by named people and kept current by the work itself.


In Sitenna, that record is baselined, owned and updated as the work happens, including by contractors in the field. Every change is logged against the person who made it. When an AI tool reads from that record, its answers are as reliable as the record behind them.


### What the MCP Connector does


Sitenna’s new MCP Connector links the enterprise AI tools your teams already use to that unified record. It’s built on the open Model Context Protocol, so Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Perplexity all connect directly, and each team keeps the tool it prefers.


Program leads ask in plain language and get an answer in seconds, from a single site up to the whole program:


- Which Cohort 1 sites are still waiting on land sign-off?
- Which critical projects could slip because of contractor delays, and who owns the fix?
- What changed on SUB-214 this week?


It works in the other direction too. Ask your AI tool to move a site to the next cohort or notify its owner, and the change is made in Sitenna under your own permissions, with a record of who did it.


For leaders, schedule risk, contractor performance and cohort progress stop being questions for next week’s report. They can be answered the moment someone needs to know.


### Your controls stay in force


Nothing stalls AI adoption faster than a security team left guessing where the data goes. The connector runs inside the permissions and audit trail you already have:


- Every connection signs in as a named user, with that person’s Sitenna permissions.
- Every change is recorded against them in the audit trail.
- The connector runs in your Sitenna region, encrypted in transit.
- It’s covered by Sitenna’s SOC 2 audit and penetration testing.
- Administrators can revoke access instantly.


Conversations stay in your own AI tool. Sitenna receives the data requests, never the prompts.


### The choice in front of leaders


Your teams will keep using AI, whatever the policy says. The real decision is whether that AI reads from scattered files or from the verified record your programs actually run on.


Connect it to the record and the answers change. They arrive just as fast, and now they’re answers you can take to your board.


Asset information you can trust, through the AI you choose.
